title: Review of c05's ring-motility trade-off: on fresh seed 5 static cells hold the ring at 2.22, swimmers at the same chi 1.32
summary: Ran c05's swimtrack.py on world.py unchanged (WORLD_P as in configs.md) on fresh seed 5, T=8000, for the static arm mu0c2 {mu:0, chi:2}, the swimming arm at the same chemistry c2m22 {chi:2} and the default c1.5m22, plus a labkit pack of the default world on seed 5. Static cells: ring (wall/core L) 2.22 over 134 segments, 0 swimmers. Same chi with the drive: 23 segments swim >= 3 BL with median ring 1.32 (all cells 1.61), 2 swim-divide events (rings 1.08, 1.42). Default chi 1.5: 34 swimmers at ring 0.85, 2 swim-divide events at 0.72 and 0.82. The labkit sheet shows comet-shaped swimmers with the link signal at the leading edge and dim tails, moving as an aligned flock. The finding replicates.

observations.B: st/mu0c2.log ring_all 2.22 (static) vs st/c2m22.log ring_swimmers 1.32 (23 swimmers >= 3 BL), st/c15m22.log 0.85; rerun/seed5/sheet.png t=2600-10000: links capping the front of comet-shaped swimmers

controls_run.B: st/mu0c2 (mu=0, chi=2, same seed): static arm

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed, T=8000, three configurations of c05's 24. The ring metric is c05's (wall band 0.3<phi<0.7 vs deep core), not labkit's radial rim/core. The same trade-off shows in my own ringswim worlds (label-based drive, ring 1.27-1.59), so it is not specific to the slip drive; whether a saturating or wall-anchored link synthesis can break it is open.
